text:
Pierre-Luc Dubois had goals in four straight games in mid-November, the run CBS Sports tracked through the Nov. 15 game against New Jersey, and then two quiet nights against Tampa Bay and Buffalo. That's the shape of his season so far: 5 goals and 12 points in 15 games for Washington, on about 16 and a half minutes a night, after a 2025-26 that ended at 29 games.

Some of it is running hot. He has scored about 1.7 more goals than his chances say he should, and his on-ice shooting luck is among the friendlier numbers on the roster. But the underlying play is real: the Capitals get about 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, more than four points better than when he sits. Evolving-Hockey had his competition last season in the 98th percentile, so those minutes come against top lines.

What to watch: whether the shot volume (25 shots in 15 games) climbs enough to carry the scoring once the finishing cools.
